items.title: Cairo Poultry stock: Nine-month profit drops 38.3% - ad-hoc-news.de
items.body: Cairo Poultry stock: Nine-month profit drops 38.3% Published on 11/16/2026 at 02:58 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS Cairo Poultry earnings overview - Consolidated revenue increased during the first nine months of 2026. - Standalone net income rose over the same period. - The company remains focused on vertically integrated poultry production in Egypt. On Thursday, November 12, 2026, Cairo Poultry reported weaker consolidated earnings for the first nine months of the year, while revenue increased. Arab Finance said the financial statements filed with the Egyptian Exchange showed consolidated net profit of EGP 1.439 billion, down 38.31 percent from EGP 2.333 billion in the same period of 2025. Revenue grows as profit declines Consolidated revenue rose to EGP 12.104 billion from EGP 11.977 billion a year earlier. The combination of higher sales and lower bottom-line earnings points to pressure elsewhere in the consolidated result, although the report does not provide a detailed cost bridge. On a standalone basis, Cairo Poultry recorded net income of EGP 291.445 million, compared with EGP 113.879 million in the first nine months of 2025. The divergent consolidated and standalone trends leave group earnings dependent on the performance of subsidiaries and the effects of consolidation. Integrated poultry business Cairo Poultry is an Egypt-based vertically integrated poultry producer spanning grandparent stock, hatcheries, farms, feed, slaughtering and processing. Its products include poultry, processed food and animal feed, with Koki as its flagship processed-chicken brand. The company operates across the production chain from breeding through retail products in the Egyptian market. Cairo Poultry key facts - Company: Cairo Poultry Company - ISIN: EGS02051C018 - Ticker: POUL.CA - Home exchange: Egyptian Exchange - Reporting period: First nine months of 2026 Egyptian equities trade within the current market reports. items.title: Cairo Poultry stock: board backs EGP 1.9 dividend proposal - ad-hoc-news.de
items.body: Cairo Poultry stock: board backs EGP 1.9 dividend proposal Published on 10/31/2026 at 01:02 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS Dividend proposal awaits shareholder vote - The board approved a proposed cash distribution and changes to the companys authorized capital. - An extraordinary general meeting will decide on the proposed measures. - The company is also considering additional business activities and has approved steps involving non-core holdings. Cairo Poultry Companys board approved a proposed dividend of 1.9 Egyptian pounds per share on October 19, 2026, according to Arab Finance. The proposal still requires approval by the companys extraordinary general meeting. Shareholders face broader agenda The board also approved setting Cairo Poultrys authorized capital at 2 billion Egyptian pounds. It agreed to consider adding new business activities to the companys scope, leaving the final decision with shareholders. The meeting agenda adds a corporate-structure angle to the proposed payout. In September, the board approved the sale of the companys stake in Aman for guarding and integrated security and the liquidation of Cairo Leasing Company, according to the same report. Integrated poultry operations Cairo Poultry describes itself as a vertically integrated poultry producer serving Egypt. Its activities cover breeding stock, hatcheries, feed production, broiler operations, processing and branded food products, including Koki. The company is listed on the Egyptian Exchange and operates from Giza, Egypt. Investors should focus next on the extraordinary general meeting and on whether shareholders approve the proposed dividend, capital framework and business-scope changes. Broader context for Egyptian equities is available in Current market reports. Cairo Poultry at a glance - Company: Cairo Poultry Company - Ticker: POUL - Exchange: Egyptian Exchange - Proposal date: October 19, 2026 - Proposed dividend: 1.9 Egyptian pounds per share - Authorized capital: 2 billion Egyptian pounds

items.title: Billionaire Paul Tudor Jones warns AI and IPOs could hit stocks hard in 2027. Protect your nest egg now - Yahoo Finance
items.body: Moneywise and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue through links in the content below. Wall Street's appetite for artificial intelligence has helped fuel a stock market boom. But billionaire investor Paul Tudor Jones is worried about what happens when the bill comes due. "2027 is going to be really, really challenging for the stock market," the Tudor Investment Corp. founder told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Oct. 13 (1). Top Picks - Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one - A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change - Gold has overtaken U.S. Treasuries as central banks' top reserve asset. Get Goldco's 2026 Precious Metals IRA Playbook for free His concern comes down to supply and demand. As companies raise money to fund the AI buildout and big names go public, more shares will compete for investors' dollars. Jones expects that shift to make life harder for shareholders — and he plans to bet on falling prices. "I'll be short the whole year," he said. If you've benefited from rising stocks, it might be worth asking how much of your nest egg depends on the boom continuing. More shares, more competition For years, corporate buybacks and acquisitions have helped take shares off the market. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) alone repurchased 402 million shares for $89.3 billion in fiscal 2025 (2). Acquisitions can also remove an entire company's stock from public trading. When Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) bought Activision Blizzard in 2023, it cancelled shareholders' stock in exchange for $95 per share in cash (3). Jones tracks those forces against the stock coming onto the market through IPOs, additional offerings and the expiration of selling restrictions. He believes that balance is becoming less favorable for investors. SpaceX's enormous valuation and the anticipated offerings from Anthropic and OpenAI are changing the calculation, he said. More companies seeking investor money could make it harder to sustain high stock prices. An IPO also isn't necessarily the end of the selling. Employees, founders and early backers often face lockup periods that temporarily prevent them from unloading their shares. Once those restrictions expire, more stock becomes available to trade. Those shareholders won't necessarily sell immediately, but buyers may eventually need to absorb substantial blocks of stock. That creates a potential share overhang (4): The prospect of selling that could weigh on prices if demand doesn't keep pace.
